title: Agenda, Time and Priorities
summary: How expanding board responsibilities collide with fixed meeting time, and how to build an agenda that gives the most important matters the attention they need.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How expanding board responsibilities collide with fixed meeting time, and how to build an agenda that gives the most important matters the attention they need.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the signs of agenda overload and its effect on scrutiny
Apply practical rules for prioritising and sequencing board business
Evaluate the trade-offs in longer, more frequent or larger board meetings
Syllabus: Agenda overload: routine reporting crowding out strategy
Sequencing, timing and protecting time for unscheduled discussion
Consent agendas, committees and deciding what not to discuss
Directors' time commitment and the risk of over-boarding
Intended Audience: Chairs, non-executive and independent directors and board committee members
Executive directors and senior managers who present to or sit on the board
Company secretaries and heads of governance responsible for board processes and evaluation
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No prior governance training is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Olivier Sibony, You're About to Make a Terrible Mistake! How Biases Distort Decision-Making (2020)
